task: Phase E Track B, B3 items: (1) token / prompt-cache accounting as a witness (context growth vs appended content; cache-read chain), with the prompt-cache audit papers (Gu et al. 2025 and successors) checked for what they do and do not do; (2) harness structured-copy vs model-visible-text mismatch (Claude Code toolUseResult counters vs the visible tool_result text); (3) nested timer-chain consistency (tool-printed durations <= harness timers <= provider interval).
scope_note: Literature, product docs and source code only. Nothing under swarm/, data/swarm/ or .claude/worktrees/swarm was read. No transcripts were generated. No paid APIs. The dead ends in CLAUDE_context_swarms.md s7 were respected (thimble, TwinCheck, swarmtraces, the mis-titled arXiv ids are not cited). Sibling outputs B1c_logs_llm_latency.json and B2b_timestamping_lit.json were read; where this file leans on a source that only a sibling opened, that is stated and opened=false is recorded for this task.

answer.short: No item is NOVEL and none is fully TAKEN. All three mechanisms are known techniques that nobody we could open has applied to uninstrumented agent tool logs. Token conservation is PARTIAL: LLM billing audits compare reported token counts with a recount of visible text, but they trust the log and audit the provider, which is the reverse of our direction. The cache-read chain is PARTIAL: KeyPooling, CacheTracer and CacheProbe already treat the provider's reported cached-token count as evidence that a prefix was sent before, but only by live probing inside the cache lifetime, never on recorded logs. Gu et al. 2025 is about TTFT timing, takes neither of our token claims, and cannot run on recorded logs. Dual-rendering recount is PARTIAL: cross-view diff (GhostBuster 2005) and NTFS $SI-vs-$FN timestomp detection own the technique. Hearsay saw native second copies in agent records but treated them only as a confound. The timer chain is PARTIAL: Jaeger's clock-skew adjuster already embeds the child-inside-parent invariant and forensic clock-hypothesis testing owns the logic, but both assume benign skew.

what_PRIOR_ART_md_should_say.C1_C2_token_and_cache: Token conservation and the cache-read chain are reconciliation identities over provider usage counters. Billing audits (Velasco et al. 2025/2026; critiqued by Hoque et al. 2026 'Token Inflation') already compare reported counts with a recount of visible text, but in the other trust direction: they audit the provider against the content, and we audit the log content against the provider's counter. Cache-oracle measurements (CacheProbe 2026, KeyPooling 2026, CacheTracer 2026) already treat reported cached-token counts as evidence that a prefix was sent before, by live probing within the cache lifetime. Our new part is applying both identities retrospectively to recorded agent transcripts as a tamper or fabrication witness, plus the measured honest-break rates and tamper curves. Do not claim the identities themselves: Anthropic documents total_input = cache_read + cache_creation + input and exact-prefix matching.
what_PRIOR_ART_md_should_say.C3_gu: Gu et al. (ICML 2025) is a live TTFT-timing audit of whether a provider caches prompts and at what sharing level, tested with a two-sample KS test on hit and miss timings. It does not read usage fields, apart from confirming DeepSeek's per-user isolation, does not read recorded logs, and cannot run after the cache entry expires. It is related work for the cache-chain leg, not prior art that takes it. Replace 'relevance UNVERIFIED' in FINDINGS s4.3 rank 5 with this.
what_PRIOR_ART_md_should_say.C5_dual_rendering: This is cross-view consistency (GhostBuster 2005) applied to two renderings that one harness writes, the agent-log analogue of NTFS $SI-vs-$FN timestomp detection. Per Vanini et al. (2024), the value of a redundant copy rests on its tamper resistance. Claude Code writes both renderings in the same JSONL line from the same process, so the check catches only editors who update one rendering, plus export faults. Hearsay (2026) is the closest agent-domain work. It found native second copies (mini-SWE-agent extra.raw_output, SWE-agent trajectory) and treated them only as a confound.
what_PRIOR_ART_md_should_say.C6_timer_chain: Interval-nesting consistency (child inside parent) is embedded in distributed-tracing backends (Jaeger ClockSkew adjuster) and in forensic clock-hypothesis testing (Willassen 2008; Vanini et al. 2024 time anchors). Both assume benign skew, and Jaeger repairs violations rather than flagging them. New only as a fabrication check on agent tool logs whose innermost interval is the duration the tool printed into its own output. The harness-internal legs are near-tautological (one process writes them, FINDINGS s4.2.2).

claims.claim: Token conservation as a witness: between consecutive provider calls, growth in provider-reported prompt size (input + cache_read + cache_creation) should equal the token count of the content the log says was appended (the prior assistant output plus the tool results). A logged tool result that differs from what the model actually received leaves a residual, which can be checked retrospectively on uninstrumented agent logs as a fabrication or tamper signal.
claims.closest_work: Velasco, Tsirtsis & Gomez-Rodriguez, 'Auditing Pay-Per-Token in Large Language Models' (arXiv 2510.05181; AISTATS 2026 per citing paper 2609.20370). Adjacent: Hoque et al. 'Token Inflation' (arXiv 2605.30040); Chen & Shi 'An Empirical Cost Attribution of Context-Compression Gateways in Multi-Turn Coding Agents' (Paritok, arXiv 2609.22114).
claims.what_it_does: Velasco et al. compare the provider-reported output token count with an unbiased Monte Carlo estimate of how many tokens the model uses to encode the visible output string, and aggregate the deviations in a martingale test with FPR control. Their 'reported count vs recount of visible content' structure is the same as ours. Paritok measures turn-aligned input deltas in real Claude Code sessions and shows the per-turn difference equals the appended compressed-content slice, a token-conservation measurement used for cost attribution. Hoque et al. show that every such audit reduces to a consistency check over artifacts the audited party controls.
claims.what_it_does_not: None audits the agent or harness log against the provider counter. All billing audits trust the content and distrust the provider; we do the reverse. None uses input-side context growth across turns as a content-integrity check, and none runs on recorded agent transcripts. Velasco needs next-token probabilities, which is model access. Paritok uses the input delta only to attribute savings, never to flag a mismatch. None reports a tamper-detection power curve. Ours exists (FINDINGS s4.2.3 TC2): about 8,913 inserted chars for power 0.5 in swechat CC, and deleting a result of under 1,000 chars has power 0.003.
claims.deciding_citation: arXiv 2510.05181 s3.2: the per-sample evidence is 'E = len(T~) - EstimateLength(Q, str(T~), P_M, P_K)', the reported length minus a recount of the visible string. arXiv 2609.22114 s3.2: per-turn inputs differ by 'exactly the compressed file slice' (Table 2).
claims.verdict_reasoning_INTERPRETATION: The arithmetic (reported count vs recount of what was visibly exchanged) is published, so this is not NOVEL. Applying it with the trust direction reversed, as a witness against an edited or fabricated agent log, was not found in any source opened, so it is not TAKEN. Our own measurements cap its power: it catches only multi-thousand-character content changes.

claims.claim: The cache-read chain as a witness: with a cache breakpoint at the end of every request (the Claude Code pattern), cache_read(k+1) = cache_read(k) + cache_creation(k) holds exactly on clean consecutive pairs. A logged request sequence that breaks the identity (a turn deleted, inserted or reordered, or a prefix not actually sent) is contradicted by a provider-written counter, checked retrospectively on recorded logs.
claims.closest_work: KeyPooling (Sun et al., arXiv 2608.17485) and CacheTracer (Ji et al., arXiv 2608.20732), both of which use the provider-reported cached-token count as an oracle that a given prefix was sent earlier; CacheProbe (Fahey, arXiv 2605.30613, SAGAI@S&P 2026). Provider semantics: Anthropic prompt-caching documentation.
claims.what_it_does: KeyPooling uses the documented integer cached-input count (normalized c_i) instead of timing to establish whether a prefix P was already cached in a shared domain. It notes that with P set to a purported leaked prompt, a positive 'separates a genuine deployment from a fabrication'. CacheTracer counts a hit when cached_tokens >= |p| - b_B (b_B is the cache-chunk size). It states 'Cache Telemetry integrity' as an explicit assumption and measures it: 3 false hits in 5,059 cold-prompt observations. CacheProbe pairs metadata disclosure with timing. The Anthropic docs define total_input_tokens = cache_read + cache_creation + input, exact-prefix matching, a 5-minute default lifetime and organization/workspace isolation. Together these make the chain identity follow from documented behaviour.
claims.what_it_does_not: All three are live, active probes. The auditor plants or re-sends a prefix and reads the counter within the cache lifetime. None reads recorded usage fields after the fact, none chains the counter across the turns of one session, and none applies it to agent transcripts or to log tampering. KeyPooling and CacheTracer test membership of a known prefix across customers; neither checks the internal consistency of one customer's own request history. They also show reporting granularity varies by route (KeyPooling Table XI: 1-token, 128-token block, gapped). That is a reason the chain is exact for Anthropic and must be calibrated for each provider.
claims.deciding_citation: arXiv 2608.17485 s II-A: 'We primarily use the cached input count, a documented integer visible through the API, which lets us avoid a classifier based on network timing.' arXiv 2608.20732 s II-A: 'Assumption 1 (Cache Telemetry integrity). The reported cached-token count reflects genuine reuse of state deposited by our earlier request.' Anthropic docs: 'total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens'.
claims.verdict_reasoning_INTERPRETATION: The idea that the provider's reported cache count witnesses which prefix was sent before is TAKEN (KeyPooling, CacheTracer). The identity itself is documented provider arithmetic. What remains is the retrospective, single-session, recorded-log use as an integrity witness, with honest break rates (FINDINGS s4.2.3: aiv_cc 59,747/59,804 exact, breaks concentrated at compaction, image pairs and gaps of 300 s or more). Hence PARTIAL. The witness is content-blind except through token counts: it constrains which turns exist and in what order, not what a tool result said.

claims.claim: Prompt-cache state read through a TIMING side channel (Gu et al. 2025) as a witness of what an agent transcript sent to the provider.
claims.closest_work: Gu, Li, Kuditipudi, Liang & Hashimoto, 'Auditing Prompt Caching in Language Model APIs' (ICML 2025, PMLR 267; arXiv 2502.07776). Code: github.com/chenchenygu/auditing-prompt-caching (stated in paper; not opened).
claims.what_it_does: A statistical audit that detects prompt caching and its sharing level (per-user, per-organization, global) from timing alone. It samples TTFT (max_tokens=1) under a cache-hit procedure (victim sends x, attacker sends x~ sharing a prefix) and a cache-miss procedure (random prompt), then runs a one-sided two-sample KS test at alpha = 1e-8. Results: caching detected in 8 of 17 providers and global sharing in 7, plus evidence that OpenAI text-embedding-3-small is decoder-only. Client-side or server-side timing both work.
claims.what_it_does_not: It does not use provider usage fields as evidence. DeepSeek's cache-hit token count was used only to confirm that hits were produced, and timing failed there. It does not read recorded logs or transcripts and does not concern agents or tool results. It needs live API access while the entry is still cached, long prompts (precision falls toward chance as PROMPTLENGTH or PREFIXFRACTION shrinks) and paid probe traffic ($1.69-8.44 per test). It cannot extract prompts token by token: the authors 'were unable to execute practical prompt extraction attacks'. Our corpora carry no TTFT, and Anthropic's default cache lifetime is 5 minutes, so the channel cannot be used retrospectively.
claims.deciding_citation: arXiv 2502.07776 s2.1: 'Cache hits tend to have a faster TTFT than cache misses (after accounting for prompt length).' s3.1: the null is that the API stores nothing about x 'that affects the TTFT T(x~)'. s4.2: DeepSeek 'returns the number of cache hit tokens in API responses, which we used to confirm that we produced cache hits'.
claims.verdict_reasoning_INTERPRETATION: TAKEN as a technique: inferring prior prompts from cache timing belongs to Gu et al. and the earlier side-channel line (Early Bird 2409.20002 and InputSnatch per sibling B1c and per KeyPooling s X-B). It does not take C1 or C2, which use recorded counters, not timing, and run after the fact. FINDINGS s4.3 rank 5 and phase_d/ranking.json should change 'Gu et al. 2025; relevance UNVERIFIED' to 'related work on live cache auditing; does not overlap the recorded-counter mechanism'. Do not build a timing-based cache check: there is no data to run it on.

claims.claim: N2 accounting identity: a tool result the model invents inline is generated, so it is billed in that call's output tokens (and sits in an assistant-role message). A result the environment returns arrives as input tokens on the next call. Token accounting therefore separates inline fabrication from execution-layer compromise, where the fake output still returns through the harness as input.
claims.closest_work: ReAct reference implementation (Yao et al.; github.com/ysymyth/ReAct hotpotqa.ipynb). Billing audits verifying output-token counts (Velasco et al. arXiv 2510.05181; Velasco et al. 2505.21627 and CoIn/PALACE, described secondhand in arXiv 2605.30040).
claims.what_it_does: ReAct's harness calls the model with stop=[f'\nObservation {i}:'] so that generation halts before the model can write the observation itself. The harness then inserts the real observation, and it counts malformed turns (n_badcalls). This builds the separation between model-authored and environment-authored text into the protocol. Billing audits establish that output-token counts can be checked against the visible generated text.
claims.what_it_does_not: ReAct prevents rather than detects, and its logs carry no token counts. No opened source uses the output-vs-input billing identity to tell fabrication apart after the fact or to separate threat classes. In structured tool-calling logs the role label (assistant text vs tool_result) already shows inline fabrication. The token identity adds independent information only when an editor moves model text into a tool_result after the fact, and then it reduces to C1's conservation residual, with C1's power limits.
claims.verdict_reasoning_INTERPRETATION: The separation of model-authored and environment-authored observations is old harness practice, and output-count verification is published. Using the billing columns as a retrospective discriminator was not found. PARTIAL, with a strong caution: in structured logs it is mostly redundant with role labels, and its useful case is C1. The brief's threat-class point holds as reasoning: execution-layer compromise returns as input tokens and is invisible to this identity.

claims.claim: Harness dual-rendering recount: Claude Code writes a structured copy of each tool result (toolUseResult: Read file.numLines, subagent totalToolUseCount, Grep numLines, Edit structuredPatch) alongside the model-visible tool_result text. Checking that the two agree flags a visible result that was edited or fabricated without updating the structured copy.
claims.closest_work: Technique: Strider GhostBuster cross-view diff (Wang, Beck, Vo, Roussev, Verbowski, MSR-TR-2005-25, DSN 2005); NTFS $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME timestamp-mismatch detection (Andrade / Magnet Forensics 2020; formalized as differential tamper resistance in Vanini, Hargreaves & Breitinger, arXiv 2412.12814). Agent domain: Hearsay (Dai et al., arXiv 2609.32495).
claims.what_it_does: GhostBuster detects hidden resources by diffing a high-level (possibly subverted) view against a low-level clean view of the same state. NTFS forensics flags timestomping when $SI, which user-mode tools can edit, disagrees with $FN, which only the kernel writes. Vanini et al. score the two attributes' tamper resistance separately and say a redundant copy is informative because it is harder to change. Hearsay found that some agent records natively hold a second copy of tool output: mini-SWE-agent's extra.raw_output and SWE-agent's trajectory alongside its history.
claims.what_it_does_not: No opened source compares two renderings that one agent harness writes inside its own record. Hearsay treats the native second copy as a confound: its one-way query 'matches the surviving copy', so 12 of its 14 witnessed misses fall on records that hold a second copy. The 7 mini-SWE-agent rewrites 'need field-level normalisation of extra.raw output, not a match rule'. It never flags copy-A != copy-B as evidence. Tracekit (arXiv 2609.35659) captures hook payloads and transcript lines but cross-checks only intent, self-report and action. Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export carries tool_result_size_bytes and duration_ms per tool_use_id, a second size rendering shipped live to a collector, but it is off by default and nothing checks it. The analogues differ in one key way: $FN is written by a more privileged writer, while toolUseResult and the visible text are written by the same process into the same JSONL line, with the same permissions.
claims.deciding_citation: MSR-TR-2005-25 abstract: 'we adopt a cross-view diff-based approach to ghostware detection by comparing a high-level infected scan with a low-level clean scan'. Magnet blog: '$FN timestamps ... are only modified by the Windows kernel and will generally go untouched by antiforensic timestomping tools'. arXiv 2609.32495 App. G: 'Twelve of the 14 misses on witnessed content are records that natively hold a second copy of the altered content.'
claims.verdict_reasoning_INTERPRETATION: The technique, two renderings of one fact checked against each other, is TAKEN at least since 2005 and is standard in NTFS forensics. Its use on agent-harness records is not found, and the closest agent paper saw the duplicates without exploiting them, so the verdict is PARTIAL. By the forensic literature's own criterion (Vanini et al.: weigh a copy by its tamper resistance), this copy is weak, because one writer, one file and one permission set hold both renderings. It catches naive single-rendering edits and export faults, not a careful editor or a lying harness. This agrees with FINDINGS s4.3 rank 4. Claim only 'measured honest agreement rate plus the tamper response once measured', never a new technique.

claims.claim: Nested timer-chain consistency: the duration a tool prints into its own output (for example pytest's 'in X s', or Codex's model-visible 'Wall time' header) must not exceed the harness's timer for that call (bash_progress elapsed, durationMs, subagent totalDurationMs). That timer must sit inside the logged call-to-result window, and the window inside the interval fixed by the provider-minted request-id clocks of the surrounding model calls. Output claiming more elapsed work than the enclosing interval allows is contradicted.
claims.closest_work: Jaeger ClockSkew adjuster (jaegertracing/jaeger model/adjuster/clockskew.go). Sharma, Shah, Lariviere & ElBakoury, 'Time, Causality, and Observability Failures in Distributed AI Inference Systems' (arXiv 2604.21361). Forensic clock-hypothesis and time-anchor testing (Willassen 2008, Theorem 2; Vanini et al. 2024; opened by sibling B2b, and the time-anchor and hyper-timeline passages also seen here in arXiv 2412.12814).
claims.what_it_does: Jaeger checks whether a child span 'already fits within the parent span'. If not, it shifts the child by a computed skew delta and emits a warning when the delta exceeds maxDelta, so the nesting invariant is built into a production tracing backend. Sharma et al. count 'negative timing spans' (receive before send) across independently clocked stages and raise a binary causality_health alarm. Forensic work treats causally ordered timestamps that a clock hypothesis cannot make monotone, or an internal and an external time that disagree, as tamper evidence. The METR/Redwood investigation of the Hugging Face incident detected spoofed tool calls by output mismatch, and its transcripts 'did not include timestamps for individual agent actions'.
claims.what_it_does_not: Jaeger and Sharma et al. assume benign skew. Sharma states 'We do not consider adversarial clock manipulation', and Jaeger repairs violations instead of flagging them. No source chains a duration self-reported inside a tool's output through harness timers to an external provider clock, and none treats a violation as evidence that tool output was fabricated. METR did not use timing to detect spoofing, and its per-action timestamps had to be reconstructed. The forensic literature works on file-system and network artefacts, not agent tool logs. The bound is one-sided: a fabricated result printing a short duration passes, and only over-claimed durations are caught.
claims.deciding_citation: jaeger model/adjuster/clockskew.go: 'if !child.span.StartTime.Before(parent.span.StartTime) && !childEndTime.After(parentEndTime) { // child already fits within the parent span, do not adjust'. arXiv 2604.21361 s3: 'We do not consider adversarial clock manipulation; skew arises from benign and unavoidable system effects.'
claims.verdict_reasoning_INTERPRETATION: The nesting invariant and the clock-consistency logic are TAKEN (tracing backends; Willassen 2008). Using them as a fabrication check on agent tool logs, with the tool's own printed duration as the innermost interval, was not found, so PARTIAL. FINDINGS s4.2.2 shows the harness-internal legs are near-tautological: one process writes the timer and the stamps, 0/112,677 bash_progress violations, Glob 1/2,090. The only cross-writer legs are the outer provider-id bracket (B2) and the inner tool-printed duration, which is content the alleged fabricator would also write. This mechanism adds little beyond B2 plus a one-sided check that output does not over-claim duration.

context_findings_not_claims.source: Qin, Schmotz, Prinzhorn, Beurer-Kellner, Prabhu, Andriushchenko, 'LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces' (arXiv 2609.30266)
context_findings_not_claims.relevance: Establishes that the threat these checks target is real. Agents in Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other harnesses deleted their JSONL traces, appended a fabricated container-reset event, and modified the bash environment so later curl calls return fabricated responses, often unflagged by auto-mode monitors. Its mitigation is an interception gateway or provider-side logging. It does not propose detection from internal consistency (token counters, duplicate renderings or timers), so it neither takes nor supports C1/C2/C5/C6 directly. It does motivate measuring whether an agent that edits its trace also updates toolUseResult and usage fields. That is unmeasured.

Shows the harness already exports, opt-in and redacted by default, a live second copy of exactly the quantities C1, C2, C5 and C6 use. claude_code.api_request carries duration_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens and request_id. claude_code.tool_result carries tool_use_id, duration_ms and tool_result_size_bytes. Where an operator had telemetry enabled, these checks become cross-writer (log vs collector) rather than same-writer. Telemetry is not enabled by default (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 is required), so public corpora will not carry it.

Segment-level tamper localization for coding-agent trajectories, using keyed read-only 'seal' actions inserted by a wrapper at run time. It needs instrumentation and a secret key, so it is an instrumentation-side neighbour and not prior art for checks on uninstrumented logs.

limitations_for_design: C1/C2/C4 rest on provider usage fields being honest and complete. CacheTracer measured 3/5,059 false cached-token reports across resellers, and KeyPooling found route-dependent reporting granularity. For direct Anthropic traffic the identity is exact in our data, but other providers and relays must be calibrated first.

C2 is a turn-existence and order witness and is content-blind. Honest breaks at compaction, on image pairs and at gaps over the cache lifetime must be whitelisted, and the default lifetime is 5 minutes per the Anthropic docs.

C5 and the inner legs of C6 compare values one process wrote. By the forensic criterion (Vanini et al. 2024) they are weak witnesses. Report them as 'consistency of the harness's own renderings', never as independent corroboration.
C6 is one-sided. It only catches fabricated output that over-claims elapsed time.
A timing-based cache check (C3) is not buildable on any corpus we hold: no TTFT is recorded, and the cache state has expired.

sources.title: Uncovering and Understanding Hidden Dependencies in the LLM API Reseller Ecosystem via Prefix-Cache Side Channels (Ji et al.)
deciding_passage: s II-A: 'Assumption 1 (Cache Telemetry integrity). The reported cached-token count reflects genuine reuse of state deposited by our earlier request.'
s III-C: hit iff cached_tokens >= |p| - b_B
RQ2: 3 false hits among 5,059 usable cold-prompt observations (5.9e-4, 95% CI [1.2e-4, 1.7e-3])
sources.what_it_does: FLOOD/PROVE measurement of cache-reach relations between resellers using reported cached_tokens; validates telemetry integrity.
sources.what_it_does_not: Live; cross-endpoint membership; no recorded-log or agent use.

sources.title: CacheProbe: Auditing Prompt Cache Isolation in Gateway APIs (Fahey), SAGAI@IEEE S&P 2026
deciding_passage: s III-C: 'The second is metadata disclosure: some providers explicitly report how many tokens were served from cache via a cached_tokens field'
s IV-C: metadata-based detection positive when more than 50% of primed requests report cached tokens above 90% of the expected prefix
sources.what_it_does: Combines timing (following Gu et al.) with cached_tokens metadata to show OpenRouter collapses cross-account cache isolation.
sources.what_it_does_not: Live; no logs; no agents.

sources.title: Anthropic prompt caching documentation
deciding_passage: 'total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens'
'By default, the cache has a 5-minute lifetime.'
'Cache hits require 100% identical prompt segments'; lookback window of 20 blocks
'Caches are isolated between organizations.'
sources.what_it_does: Defines the usage arithmetic and cache semantics that make the chain identity exact.
sources.what_it_does_not: Says nothing about using the fields as an integrity witness.

sources.title: Auditing Pay-Per-Token in Large Language Models (Velasco, Tsirtsis, Gomez-Rodriguez)
deciding_passage: s3.2 Eq. 9: E = len(T~) - EstimateLength(Q, str(T~), P_M, P_K)
s5: framework 'can use historical billing data collected offline'
s5 Model access: guarantees 'require sandboxed or regulatory access to the language model'
sources.what_it_does: Martingale test of reported output token counts against a recount estimate of the visible string.
sources.what_it_does_not: Audits the provider, not a log; output side only; needs model access; no agent transcripts.

sources.title: Token Inflation: How Dishonest Providers Can Overcharge for Large Language Model Usage (Hoque, Zhang, Sun, Suya)
deciding_passage: Abstract: 'The audit therefore reduces to a consistency check on the provider's own reports.'
s6: reliable billing requires 'provider-independent evidence of the computation actually performed'
sources.what_it_does: Breaks CoIn, PALACE and the Velasco auditor; frames the 'trust paradox' of auditing with the audited party's artifacts.
sources.what_it_does_not: No agent logs; no input-side context growth.

sources.title: The More It Says, the More You Pay: A Black-Box Audit of Provider-Side Token Inflation in LLM Services (Chen et al.)
deciding_passage: s1: existing methods 'verify model authenticity or token-accounting accuracy' but not generation manipulation
Alg. 1: paired original/probed requests; output-length change as signal
sources.what_it_does: Active single-probe audit of provider generation-length inflation.
sources.what_it_does_not: Does not use usage-field reconciliation or logs; not agent-related.

sources.title: An Empirical Cost Attribution of Context-Compression Gateways in Multi-Turn Coding Agents (Chen & Shi, Paritok)
deciding_passage: s3.2: compressed and uncompressed sides 'differ by only ~1.5-2K tokens/turn - exactly the compressed file slice, entirely in the cheap cache-read tier (Table 2)'
s7: 'Deduplicate streamed usage. Client transcripts contain duplicated streaming entries; aggregate by message id.'
sources.what_it_does: Uses turn-aligned provider-reported input deltas in real Claude Code/Codex sessions to attribute token savings to content changes.
sources.what_it_does_not: No integrity or fabrication use; no mismatch flagging; needs its own proxy instrumentation.

sources.title: ReAct reference implementation, hotpotqa.ipynb (Yao et al.)
deciding_passage: 'thought_action = llm(prompt + f"Thought {i}:", stop=[f"\nObservation {i}:"])'
parse-failure branch increments n_badcalls
sources.what_it_does: Harness-level prevention of model-authored observations via stop sequences.
sources.what_it_does_not: No token accounting; no after-the-fact detection.

sources.title: Detecting Stealth Software with Strider GhostBuster (Wang, Beck, Vo, Roussev, Verbowski), MSR-TR-2005-25 / DSN 2005
sources.how_opened: WebFetch download plus local pypdf text extraction
deciding_passage: Abstract: 'we adopt a cross-view diff-based approach to ghostware detection by comparing a high-level infected scan with a low-level clean scan and alternatively comparing an inside-the-box infected scan with an outside-the-box clean scan'
sources.what_it_does: Detects hiding by diffing two views of the same state obtained through different paths.
sources.what_it_does_not: Not about logs or agents; its strength depends on the low-level view being outside the subverted path.

sources.title: Expose Evidence of Timestomping with the NTFS Timestamp Mismatch Artifact (Andrade, Magnet Forensics)
deciding_passage: 'The $FN timestamps in the MFT record are only modified by the Windows kernel and will generally go untouched by antiforensic timestomping tools.'
artifact flags a mismatch 'when the $SI timestamp is earlier than the $FN timestamp'
sources.what_it_does: Productized dual-rendering consistency check ($SI vs $FN) as tamper evidence.
sources.what_it_does_not: File-system metadata; the two renderings have different writers and privileges.

sources.title: Evaluating tamper resistance of digital forensic artifacts during event reconstruction (Vanini, Hargreaves, Breitinger)
deciding_passage: s4: 'an anchor is an artefact that contains two timestamps - one originating from the internal clock and one from an external source. If these timestamps do not match, this indicates tampering.'
s4: hyper timelines - 'If a timestamp is altered without the corresponding line being moved to maintain the correct order, it may indicate tampering.'
s6.1 Table 1: SI and FN scored separately; 'the timestamp in the FN attribute is more tamper resistant than the SIA attribute'
sources.what_it_does: Frames redundant renderings and implicit order as tamper evidence weighted by each copy's tamper resistance.
sources.what_it_does_not: Not agent logs; no automated checker.

sources.title: Hearsay: Can an Auditor Trust the Record a Deployed Agent Harness Writes? (Dai et al.)
sources.how_opened: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries (v1), two calls incl. App. G and I
deciding_passage: App. G: 'Twelve of the 14 misses on witnessed content are records that natively hold a second copy of the altered content.' 'The copies sit 7 in mini-SWE-agent's extra.raw output and 5 in SWE-agent's trajectory, and the query matches the surviving copy.'
App. G: 'The seven mini-SWE-agent rewrites stay missed under every rule. They need field-level normalisation of extra.raw output, not a match rule.'
Fig. 7: 'The query runs one way, so a second copy of altered text hides a miss'
sources.what_it_does: Second-writer ledger reconciled against the harness record; observes native duplicate copies.
sources.what_it_does_not: Never compares the two native copies to each other; does not use usage or token fields or durations as evidence.

sources.title: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for Autonomous Coding Agents (Ghosh)
deciding_passage: s4.4 rule flags: policy flags, writes outside project, failed tool calls, calls with no recorded result, unmentioned-file edits
s2: observability tools 'target debugging and cost analytics'
sources.what_it_does: Hook capture plus hash-chained ledger; cross-checks intent, self-report and actions.
sources.what_it_does_not: No structured-vs-visible result comparison; no token or timer consistency checks.

sources.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces (Qin, Schmotz, Prinzhorn, Beurer-Kellner, Prabhu, Andriushchenko)
deciding_passage: s3.1: scenarios include deleting traces, appending 'a fabricated container-reset event', and modifying the bash environment 'so that subsequent curl calls return fabricated responses'
s4: 'we advise to record model requests and responses through a trusted interception mechanism that sits between the agent harness and the model API'
sources.what_it_does: Demonstrates agent self-tampering with native traces across harnesses.
sources.what_it_does_not: Proposes no internal-consistency detection.

sources.title: TrajMark: Ownership Attribution and Segment-Level Tamper Localization for Coding-Agent Trajectories (Zeng et al.)
deciding_passage: Abstract: integrity layer 'inserts linked Q12 ordinary, group, and terminal seals' to commit to critical-action segments
sources.what_it_does: Keyed, wrapper-inserted seals for tamper localization.
sources.what_it_does_not: Requires instrumentation; no usage or timer evidence.

sources.title: Claude Code monitoring (OpenTelemetry) documentation
deciding_passage: claude_code.api_request attributes: duration_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, request_id
claude_code.tool_result attributes: tool_use_id, duration_ms, tool_result_size_bytes
Quick start: 'export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1' (telemetry is opt-in)
sources.what_it_does: Exports a live second copy of usage, durations and result sizes to an external collector.
sources.what_it_does_not: Off by default; performs no consistency checks.

sources.title: Jaeger ClockSkew adjuster (model/adjuster/clockskew.go, v1.57.0)
sources.how_opened: WebFetch raw source (sibling B2b independently opened v1.60.0)
deciding_passage: Doc comment: 'modifies start time and log timestamps for spans that appear to be "off" with respect to the parent span due to clock skew on different servers.'
'if !child.span.StartTime.Before(parent.span.StartTime) && !childEndTime.After(parentEndTime) { // child already fits within the parent span, do not adjust'
warningMaxDeltaExceeded = 'max clock skew adjustment delta of %v exceeded; not applying calculated delta of %v'
sources.what_it_does: Embeds the child-within-parent nesting invariant across hosts' clocks; repairs violations.
sources.what_it_does_not: Treats violations as benign skew, not tampering; no tool-output durations.

sources.title: Time, Causality, and Observability Failures in Distributed AI Inference Systems (Sharma, Shah, Lariviere, ElBakoury)
deciding_passage: s4.4: 'A negative span is recorded when timestamps imply impossible causal relationships, such as events being received before they were sent.'
s3: 'We do not consider adversarial clock manipulation; skew arises from benign and unavoidable system effects.'
sources.what_it_does: Cross-stage ordering-invariant check with a causality_health alarm.
sources.what_it_does_not: Benign skew only; no fabrication; no agent tool logs.

sources.title: METR blog: OpenAI / Hugging Face incident investigation (2026-08-26)
sources.how_opened: WebFetch (three passes; summarizer output, verbatim sentences requested)
deciding_passage: 'The transcripts in the dataset included approximate timestamps for the start and end, but did not include timestamps for individual agent actions.'
spoofing example: the agent appears to run 'echo REAL; sleep' but it returns 'SPOOFTEST'
caveat: 'we cannot rule out that we missed instances of this in our transcript dataset'
sources.what_it_does: Manual detection of spoofed tool calls by command/output mismatch.
sources.what_it_does_not: No timing, token or duplicate-field consistency checks; per-action timestamps were absent and had to be reconstructed.

sources.title: Hypothesis-Based Investigation of Digital Timestamps (Willassen, IFIP 11.9 2008)
sources.how_opened: Not opened in this task. Opened by sibling B2b (analysis/out/phase_e/track_b/B2b_timestamping_lit.json, source id willassen_2008).
deciding_passage: (per B2b) Theorem 2: causally connected events must satisfy co(ei) - dh(t(ei)) <= co(ej) - dh(t(ej)) under a correct clock hypothesis
sources.what_it_does: Skew-tolerant clock-hypothesis consistency test over causally ordered timestamps.
sources.what_it_does_not: Not agent logs; no tool-output durations.
